title: Committee of Supply – Head V (Ministry of Trade and Industry)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head V (Ministry of Trade and Industry)

sections.label: Singapore economic exposure to China
sections.summary: China's GDP grew fourfold since 2003 and Singapore's trade with China nearly quadrupled, prompting a question on managing economic exposure to China.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: China's gross domestic product (GDP) has increased fourfold since 2003 and its share of the global GDP has more than doubled from 9% to 19%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Singapore's trade with China has also increased almost four times since 2003.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Even in the area of tourism, the Chinese tourists account for about 20% of Singapore's total international visitor arrivals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask the Minister as to how we can manage our economic exposure to China, balancing the opportunities versus the risks.

sections.label: Singapore enterprise development diversity
sections.summary: Singapore has more than 200,000 enterprises of every size, growth stage, productivity capability, resource absorption and value-add to the economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Next, on enterprise development, there are more than 200,000 enterprises in Singapore and they come in every size, different stages of growth, uneven productivity capabilities and resource adsorptions and varying value-add to the economy.

sections.label: Pro-Enterprise Panel formation
sections.summary: The Pro-Enterprise Panel was formed in 2000 as a platform for companies to give feedback on regulations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The Pro-Enterprise Panel (PEP) was formed in 2000 as a platform for companies to provide feedback on regulations.

sections.label: Workforce capabilities and SkillsFuture support
sections.summary: A question asks how Government will support company involvement in building workforce capabilities, welcoming the SkillsFuture Mid-Career Support Package and hiring incentives for local jobseekers aged 40 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In that regard, can I ask how would the Government promote and support more of such involvement by companies to build their workforce capabilities?

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I applaud the Government for introducing the SkillsFuture Mid-Career Support Package.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: It is another manifestation of the Government's commitment that economic growth must, ultimately, translate to good jobs and good outcomes for all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I hope that the hiring incentive to employers who hire local jobseekers aged 40 and above, through reskilling programmes, would appeal to employers and also change their mindsets.

sections.label: Stabilisation and Support Package measures
sections.summary: The Stabilisation and Support Package tackles weaker business cash flow and saving jobs through the Jobs Support Scheme, rental waivers, rebates and temporary bridging loans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The Stabilisation and Support Package has rightly focused on tackling two critical situations: firstly, the weaker cash flow position of businesses and, secondly, to focus on saving jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The announced measures of Jobs Support Scheme, rental waivers, rebates, temporary bridging loans, among others, are relevant and practical relief measures to help businesses, especially in managing the tighter cash flow situations.

sections.label: Year-to-year economic growth plateauing
sections.summary: The economy is growing 1.5% to 2.5% year-to-year, described as plateauing though in better shape than other economies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: On a year-to-year basis, growing at 1.5% to 2.5%, we are sort of plateauing, although we are in better shape to do better than other economies.

sections.label: FTAs and MRA enhancement
sections.summary: Singapore has signed more than 25 bilateral and multilateral FTAs, and the Market Readiness Assistance scheme will be enhanced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: But in not so good times, let us say, for example, right now, how do FTAs play a part?

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We have more than 25 FTAs signed so far – bilateral and multilateral.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: One of the schemes that is also a beneficiary out of it is the Market Readiness Assistance (MRA).

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I am glad to know that the MRA will be enhanced.

sections.label: MRA enhancements for SMEs
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Ministry what the MRA enhancements are and whether funds can move to knowledge for SMEs overseas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: This is most valuable to the SMEs and businesses which want to venture overseas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: So, can I know from the Ministry what are the enhancements of the MRA, and are we able to move from funds to knowledge that can be imparted to facilitate the growth of SMEs overseas?

sections.label: Disruptive technologies in ASEAN manufacturing
sections.summary: A McKinsey Global Institute study projects disruptive technologies could create US$25 billion to $45 billion of annual output value in ASEAN by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In a study by the McKinsey Global Institute, especially for the manufacturing sector, disruptive technologies are projected to have huge economic impact, potentially creating US$25 billion to $45 billion of annual output value in ASEAN by 2030.

sections.label: SBF strategic planning session for TACs
sections.summary: In July 2019 the Singapore Business Federation held the inaugural Strategic Planning Session for TACs, attended by over 70 leaders from more than 40 TACs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In July 2019, the Singapore Business Federation (SBF) organised the inaugural Strategic Planning Session for TACs which was attended by over 70 leaders from more than 40 TACs.

sections.label: Manufacturing Alliance for Industry 4.0
sections.summary: SMF, SIAA and SGTECH formed a Manufacturing Alliance in October 2019 to help SMEs adopt modular packages for Industry 4.0.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On the manufacturing front, the Singapore Manufacturing Federation (SMF), the Singapore Industrial Automation Association (SIAA), and SGTECH have come together to form a Manufacturing Alliance in October 2019 to specialise in business model and process re-engineering, software and digitalisation as well as robotics and automation matters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Manufacturing Alliance works with an ecosystem of partners, such as Government agencies, institutes of higher learning, Centres of Innovation (COIs) and so on, to scope problem statements and curate standardised, modular implementation packages that are easy for SMEs to adopt to make progress on their journey towards Industry 4.0.

sections.label: SME Centres and FTA review
sections.summary: The speaker asks about making SME Centres more visible and about reviewing implemented FTAs' net economic impact and feedback channels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: My question to the Minister then is what can we do to make SME Centres more visible, such that we make it clear to SMEs that we have people ready and able to help them in their business journeys?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Sir, Singapore has 23 implemented FTAs and may conclude other FTAs in future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Every FTA negotiation involves making a determination on how much improved market access to give foreign companies in exchange for market access for Singapore companies in that foreign country.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Does the Government also review implemented FTAs to assess the net economic impact of the concessions given in respect of market access to foreign firms inter-corporate transferee rights and other concessions as well as whether market access for a Singapore firm has, in fact, materialised as envisaged under the FTA?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Lastly, is there a mechanism for local firms to easily give feedback on FTA-related matters and can some feedback channel be indicated on the FTA section of MTI's website?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: What processes are used to assess the net economic impact of FTAs after they are enacted?

sections.label: Market Readiness Assistance grant
sections.summary: The Market Readiness Assistance grant and Enterprise Grow Package will be enhanced with greater funding support and coverage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Fortunately, there is already the Market Readiness Assistance grant that was first introduced in 2013 to help businesses enter new markets, and also the newly announced Enterprise Grow Package.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I am glad to note that those will now be enhanced with greater funding support and coverage.

sections.label: TAC roles in internationalisation
sections.summary: It asks what other roles TACs can play in pooling knowledge and resources to help businesses seeking to internationalise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: What other roles can TACs play in pooling knowledge and resources, both locally and in-market, to help businesses seeking to internationalise?

sections.label: Expanding CTP support
sections.summary: The Ministry should consider expanding CTP and resources to transfer capabilities from foreign employees to local workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Ministry should consider expanding CTP and providing more resources to support the transfer of capabilities from foreign employees, who are already employed in Singapore, to local workers, with the aim of localising jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Funding support for CTP should be expanded to include salary and training support for local specialists, as well as Singaporean trainees on overseas attachments to acquire new capabilities.

sections.label: Government help for workers
sections.summary: It asks how MTI can share how the Government helps workers remain employable and industry-relevant, especially mature and mid-career workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Despite these major challenges, it is very heartening that our Government is taking this issue by the horns for many years now, not just within MTI but whole-of-Government, and also to do it in a tripartite manner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Therefore, can MTI share how the Government can help workers remain employable and industry-relevant in this rapidly changing environment, especially mature and mid-career workers, many in their 40s and 50s?

sections.label: Firms embracing workforce transformation
sections.summary: It asks how the Government encourages firms to see workforce transformation as complementing enterprise transformation and supports firms investing in training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can MTI share how our Government encourage more firms to embrace a mindset shift to see workforce transformation as a critical complement to enterprise transformation?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Accordingly, how can the Government support and incentivise more firms, especially SMEs, to invest in training and redesigning jobs for workers?

sections.label: Amazon career choice programme
sections.summary: Amazon's career choice programme helps workers gain skills outside Amazon's needs through resources and work flexibility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Amazon's career choice programme helps workers to gain skills in areas outside of Amazon's needs by providing resources and work flexibility.

sections.label: PMET, startup and deep-tech programmes
sections.summary: Programmes nurture local PMET and leadership talent, and an additional $300 million goes to deep-tech, including agri-tech.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: A number of programmes have been launched to nurture local PMET and leadership talent, such as the Youth Future Leaders' Programme by the Economic Development Board (EDB) and the National Trades Union Congress, the SkillsFuture Leadership Development Initiative as well as the Enterprise Singapore-ASEAN Leadership programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Sir, every year, we put a lot of emphasis on encouraging startups, either catalysing more startups in different areas in terms of tech or tech transformation, but also in creating the hardware, for example, the Launchpad and several other places where it is clean-tech startup areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: That is very encouraging and it is good to know that, this year, we are putting an additional $300 million into deep-tech and with some focus on a couple of key areas, including agri-tech.

sections.label: Overall productivity growth
sections.summary: Overall productivity rose to 2.6% per year over the last three years, up from 2.2% previously.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Overall productivity rose to 2.6% per year over the last three years, up from 2.2% in the preceding three-year period.

sections.label: MAS Fintech and regulatory sandbox
sections.summary: MAS developed the Fintech sector and a regulatory sandbox, which other sectors can emulate to support innovation trials with safeguards.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: The Monetary Authority of Singapore's (MAS’) success in developing the Fintech sector and in instituting the concept of "regulatory sandbox" to spur innovation of new technology is also something that other sectors can emulate to support experimentation and trials of promising innovations, with all the necessary safeguards.

sections.label: Singapore technology startup ecosystem
sections.summary: Singapore has 3,800 technology startups, and deep-tech startups need larger investments and longer gestation periods with higher risks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat spoke about the vibrant startup ecosystem in his Budget Speech.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: There are now 3,800 technology startups in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Deep-tech startups in emerging technology areas, such as agri-food tech, can grow to become globally competitive.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: However, these same startups also require larger investments, longer gestation periods, and not every investor has the stomach for the higher risks that come with this.

sections.label: Job losses to new technology
sections.summary: McKinsey Global Institute says up to 800 million global workers will lose jobs to new technology by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: According to the McKinsey Global Institute, up to 800 million global workers will lose their jobs to new technology by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: Earlier on, Deloitte and the University of Oxford predicted that 35% of the jobs in the United Kingdom in 2014 would go to robots in 30 years.

sections.label: Singapore natural gas imports
sections.summary: Indonesia supplies 85% of imported natural gas in gaseous form, and will stop natural gas exports to Singapore from Sumatra in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: Indonesia accounts for 85% of imported natural gas in gaseous form, with the remainder coming from Malaysia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: Pipeline natural gas has been supplemented by imports of liquified natural gas (LNG) for some years now from diverse source countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: However, Indonesia has announced that it is to stop natural gas exports to Singapore from Sumatra in 2023.

sections.label: Climate challenge as economic structural challenge
sections.summary: Minister Chan Chun Sing said the climate challenge is an economic structural challenge, and the IMF opined carbon prices should rise to US$75 per tonne by 2030 in large emitting countries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Chairman, climate challenge is an economic structural challenge for Singapore, noted Minister Chan Chun Sing, who further added that, I quote, "If we cannot manage that, we cannot even attract the industries to create the jobs for the next generation." The International Monetary Fund recently opined that price on carbon should rise to US$75 per tonne by 2030 in large emitting countries, placing constraints and pressures on fossil fuel-based industries, Yet, new energy technologies are currently available.

sections.label: Paris Accord GHG reduction requirements
sections.summary: Meeting the 2015 Paris Accord commitment on Greenhouse Gases requires changes in societal behaviours, Government regulations, industrial engagement and technology development.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: To achieve the commitment in the 2015 Paris Accord of reducing Greenhouse Gases (GHG), it will require changes in societal behaviours, Government regulations, industrial engagement and technology development.

sections.label: Sustainability in ITMs and emission platform
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether MTI will include sustainability as a fifth ITM pillar and create a platform for exchanging emission reduction best practices.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: As such, our ITMs, which are the roadmaps for growth and competitiveness for our industries, should include sustainability as an essential component of their workplan and transformation.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Will MTI consider including sustainability as a fifth pillar of the ITMs?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Relatedly, will MTI consider creating a platform to facilitate exchange of best practices for emission reduction across all major sectors of Singapore's economy, given the success of tripartite collaborations like the Singapore Packaging Agreement?

sections.label: Mandatory evaluation for productivity schemes
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Ministry could develop a mandatory programme evaluation framework for all major productivity enhancement schemes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry develop a mandatory programme evaluation framework for all major productivity enhancement schemes?

sections.label: SMEs employment and economic contribution
sections.summary: In Singapore, SMEs account for an estimated two-thirds of all employment and contribute almost S$200 billion to the economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, in Singapore, SMEs account for an estimated two-thirds of all employment and contribute almost S$200 billion to the economy.

sections.label: Grooming 900 business leaders
sections.summary: The Budget Statement talks about grooming 900 business leaders over the next three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo
sentences.text: The Budget Statement talks about grooming 900 business leaders over the next three years.

sections.label: Scale-up Programme eligibility question
sections.summary: Asks whether the Scale-up Programme, which comprises mostly large companies, would include small- and medium-sized enterprises with larger weightage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: The Scale-up Programme today, if I am not wrong, actually comprises most of the very large companies or companies that have above $100 million in revenue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: Would the Scale-up Programme include these enterprises as well, from the small- to the medium-sized, and have a larger weightage for them?

sections.label: Support for heartland enterprises digitising
sections.summary: Requests the Ministry provide additional support to help heartland enterprises adopt digitalisation and go online.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck
sentences.text: Would the Ministry consider looking at the heartland enterprises and look at the software aspect to actually put in the funding to help them?

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This crisis provides an opportunity and the motivation for our smaller, especially the simpler and more traditional, businesses and enterprises to adopt digitalisation for their operations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: However, many of these business owners would need help and I would like to request that the Ministry provide the additional support to our heartland enterprises to digitise and go online.

sections.label: Action against mask overpricing retailers
sections.summary: Asks what action would be taken against recalcitrant retailers selling face masks at substantially higher prices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Recently, there were several complaints regarding retailers selling face masks at substantially higher prices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: What action would be taken against such recalcitrant retailers?

sections.label: Amending CPFTA for financial penalties
sections.summary: Asks whether the Government would amend the CPFTA to let CCCS impose administrative financial penalties instead of only seeking injunctions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Will the Government consider amending the CPFTA to allow CCCS to have wider options of imposing administrative financial penalties instead of the current option of only seeking an injunction against egregious businesses?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The Competition Act has a financial penalty framework; perhaps a similar framework can be introduced for CPFTA.

sections.label: Fall in international visitor arrivals
sections.summary: States that international visitor arrivals may fall by more than 25% this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: International visitor arrivals may fall by more than 25% this year.

sections.label: COVID-19 economic impact versus SARS
sections.summary: States the eventual economic impact of COVID-19 could be worse than SARS given China's share of global GDP and manufacturing value added.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The eventual economic impact of COVID-19 could be worse than SARS as China now accounts for more than 19% of global gross domestic product (GDP) and 27% of global manufacturing value added.

sections.label: Jobs Support and Wage Credit
sections.summary: The $1.3 billion Jobs Support Scheme and $1.1 billion Wage Credit Scheme enhancement will safeguard employment and wage growth.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The $1.3 billion Jobs Support Scheme and the $1.1 billion enhancement of the Wage Credit Scheme will safeguard employment and wage growth.

sections.label: Tourism Recovery Action Task Force
sections.summary: The Singapore Tourism Board formed a Tourism Recovery Action Task Force of private and public sector leaders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The Singapore Tourism Board (STB) has formed a Tourism Recovery Action Task Force (TRAC) comprising leaders from both the private and public sectors.

sections.label: Connectivity, FTAs and RCEP
sections.summary: Singapore must enhance its connectivity hub value, expand FTAs, and hopes to sign an ASEAN-RCEP agreement this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: To emerge stronger globally, Singapore must continually enhance our value as a connectivity hub.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We need to adapt to changing supply chains by expanding and upgrading our network of Free Trade Agreements (FTAs).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: If all goes well, we hope to sign this agreement by the end of this year to deepen connections between the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and other RCEP Participating Countries, which together account for almost 30% of global GDP.

sections.label: Singapore's 25 FTAs
sections.summary: In response to Mr Teo Ser Luck's question, Singapore's 25 FTAs are with economies representing over 85% of global GDP.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: In response to Mr Teo Ser Luck's question, our 25 FTAs are with economies that represent more than 85% of global GDP.

sections.label: Digital Economy Agreement negotiations
sections.summary: DEA provides a trusted trade environment by guarding against digital barriers and addressing emerging technology issues; negotiations with Chile and New Zealand substantially concluded.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: By guarding against digital barriers and by addressing issues that arise from emerging technology, such as AI, DEA provides a trusted environment for trade in the digital era.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: I am pleased to note that we have substantially concluded DEA negotiations with Chile and New Zealand.

sections.label: Extended Market Readiness Assistance support
sections.summary: The enhanced 70% support under the Market Readiness Assistance will be extended another three years till 31 March 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: First, we will extend the enhanced 70% support under the Market Readiness Assistance (MRA) for another three years till 31 March 2023.

sections.label: Double Tax Deduction Scheme extension
sections.summary: The Double Tax Deduction Scheme for Internationalisation will be extended for another five years until 31 December 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Second, we will extend the Double Tax Deduction Scheme for Internationalisation (DTDi) for another five years till 31 December 2025.

sections.label: Funding for emerging technology startups
sections.summary: $300 million has been earmarked to support startups in key emerging technology areas like pharmbio and advanced manufacturing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Going forward, we must do more to translate Singapore’s research edge into an economic advantage.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We have earmarked $300 million to support startups in key emerging technology areas like pharmbio and advanced manufacturing.

sections.label: Enterprise Leadership for Transformation Programme
sections.summary: The new Enterprise Leadership for Transformation (ELT) Programme is an example of such dedicated support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: An example of such dedicated support is the new Enterprise Leadership for Transformation (ELT) Programme.

sections.label: PMET workforce and income growth
sections.summary: Over half the local workforce are PMETs, PMET jobs rose from about 1.2 million in 2016 to 1.3 million in 2019, and real median income grew 3.7% per annum from 2016 to 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: More than half of our local workforce is made up of professionals, managers, executives and technicians (PMETs).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: This is one of the highest proportions in the whole world, and the number of PMET jobs continues to rise, from about 1.2 million in 2016 to 1.3 million in 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Real median income for Singaporeans grew at 3.7% per annum from 2016 to 2019, which is higher than the 3.2% per annum in the preceding three years.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Leadership Development Initiative support
sections.summary: The SkillsFuture Leadership Development Initiative has supported over 1,000 Singaporeans in acquiring corporate leadership competencies and experiences.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Mr Leon Perera would be pleased to know that the SkillsFuture Leadership Development Initiative (LDI) has supported over 1,000 Singaporeans in acquiring corporate leadership competencies and experiences.

sections.label: Re-entry rates after retrenchment
sections.summary: In 2018, only 58.6% of resident workers aged 40 and above re-entered the workforce within six months after retrenchment, lower than 70% for those in their 30s.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: In 2018, only 58.6% of resident workers aged 40 and above managed to re-enter the workforce within six months after retrenchment, lower than the 70% for those in their 30s.

sections.label: Mid-Career Support Package job placements
sections.summary: The SkillsFuture Mid-Career Support Package targets doubling annual job placements for locals in their 40s and 50s to 5,500 by 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Through the SkillsFuture Mid-Career Support Package, we have set ourselves the target to double the annual job placements for locals in their 40s and 50s to 5,500 by 2025.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit and worker outcomes
sections.summary: Eligible employers get a one-off $10,000 SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit covering up to 90% of out-of-pocket expenses, and from 1 April worker outcomes are a mandatory condition for Enterprise Development Grant funding.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Under the SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit (SFEC), eligible employers will receive a one-off $10,000 credit to cover up to 90% of out-of-pocket expenses for supportable enterprise development and workforce transformation programmes, including reskilling and job redesign.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: My colleague, Senior Minister of State Chee Hong Tat, will elaborate.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: This is also why, from 1 April this year, worker outcomes will be included as a mandatory condition for companies that apply for Enterprise Development Grant (EDG) funding.

sections.label: Salary support for eligible workers
sections.summary: For each eligible worker, the Government will provide 20% salary support for six months, capped at $6,000 in total.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: For each eligible worker, the Government will provide 20% salary support for six months, capped at $6,000 in total.

sections.label: Standing together for Singapore's future
sections.summary: The journey ahead has opportunities and challenges, but standing together the Government, businesses, unions and citizens can overcome challenges and chart a better future for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The journey ahead is full of both opportunities and challenges.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: But if we stand together – the Government, businesses, unions and citizens – I am certain we can overcome any challenge and emerge stronger to chart a better future for all in Singapore.

sections.label: COIs supported projects
sections.summary: The COIs have supported over 4,200 projects in areas such as technical consultancy, product development and IP commercialisation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The COIs have supported over 4,200 such projects in areas, such as technical consultancy, product development and IP commercialisation.

sections.label: Startup SG Equity private funding
sections.summary: Over four years, schemes like Startup SG Equity catalysed over $560 million in private sector funding into Singapore-based startups for product development and market entry.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Over the past four years, through schemes like Startup SG Equity, the Government has catalysed over $560 million in private sector funding into Singapore-based startups, helping them with product development and bringing these products to market.

sections.label: Startup SG Equity Scheme enhancement
sections.summary: The Startup SG Equity Scheme is enhanced with a S$300 million top-up and doubled maximum funding of S$8 million per startup.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: But when they do, when these moonshot projects succeed, they break new ground and give fertile foundation for future incremental innovations to succeed thereafter.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: We will, therefore, enhance the Startup SG Equity Scheme to help our deep-tech startups in the areas of pharmaceuticals, biotech and medtech, advanced manufacturing and agri-food tech.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: To ensure they have the necessary resources to bring their products to market, Deputy Prime Minister Heng shared during the Budget that we will be topping up S$300 million to the scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: We will also enhance the scheme to double the maximum amount each startup can receive, from S$4 million to S$8 million.

sections.label: Micron and Infineon factories
sections.summary: Micron and Infineon joined the World Economic Forum's Global Lighthouse network as trail blazers earlier this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Two of Singapore's factories, Micron and Infineon, joined the World Economic Forum's Global Lighthouse network as trail blazers earlier this year.

sections.label: SIRI Assessments by companies
sections.summary: More than 250 companies have undergone SIRI Assessments, and about 30% of them were SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Since then, more than 250 companies have undergone the SIRI Assessments and, among them, about 30% were SMEs.

sections.label: JID job creation estimate
sections.summary: Over the next 20 years, companies in the JID are estimated to create 95,000 new jobs in research and advanced manufacturing.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Over the next 20 years, companies in the JID are estimated to create 95,000 new jobs in research and advanced manufacturing activities.

sections.label: New SIMTECH Innovation Factory
sections.summary: A new SIMTECH Innovation Factory will be launched in JID to boost local companies' innovation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: To build on these efforts and give more local companies a boost in innovation, I am happy to share that we will launch a new SIMTECH Innovation Factory in JID.

sections.label: Energy and Chemicals sector contribution
sections.summary: The Energy and Chemicals sector contributed 2.3% of GDP and employed around 26,000 workers in 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The Energy and Chemicals sector is a valued pillar of Singapore's economy, contributing 2.3% of our GDP and employing around 26,000 workers in 2019.

sections.label: LNG terminal gas capacity
sections.summary: The LNG terminal can cover all gas demand even if piped natural gas supply ceased today.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Our liquified natural gas (LNG) terminal has the capacity to cover all our gas demand even if our piped natural gas supply were to cease today.

sections.label: Jurong Island Circular Economy Study
sections.summary: JTC and agencies are conducting a study mapping water, energy and waste flows on Jurong Island.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: JTC is thus partnering companies on Jurong Island and other Government agencies, such as the National Environment Agency and the Public Utilities Board, to conduct a Jurong Island Circular Economy Study.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The study will map out flows of water, energy and waste on the island and identify system-level gaps.

sections.label: Agri-Food Innovation Park in Sungei Kadut
sections.summary: Phase One infrastructure works for the Agri-Food Innovation Park have started, with companies welcomed by first half of next year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Last year, I announced that we will establish an Agri-Food Innovation Park (AFIP) in Sungei Kadut to allow leading high-tech farming operators to testbed and commercialise their technologies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Infrastructure and land preparation works for Phase One of AFIP have started and we will be ready to welcome companies by the first half of next year.

sections.label: Food Regulatory Connectivity Initiative
sections.summary: An interagency workgroup develops Singapore as a trusted food trading hub and improves market access for food exports.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: This is why we have started an interagency workgroup, the Food Regulatory Connectivity Initiative, to develop Singapore as a trusted food trading hub.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: We will work with trading partners to boost recognition of Singapore’s food regulatory system and improve market access for food produced in or exported through Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: We are also partnering accredited private bodies based in Singapore to provide the necessary checks that fulfil foreign import requirements.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: For example, we are engaging China's regulators on the recognition of meat and seafood products.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: This will help Singapore companies to export their food products to new markets which previously did not permit this.

sections.label: Strengthening innovation ecosystem
sections.summary: Singapore will continue strengthening its innovation ecosystem and transforming industries through innovation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: In the years to come, we will continue to strengthen our innovation ecosystem and transform our industries through innovation so that Singapore and Singaporeans can continue to thrive.

sections.label: Employer credits for transformation programmes
sections.summary: Eligible employers receive $10,000 in credits valid three years to cover up to 90% of transformation programme expenses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Each eligible employer will be given $10,000 in credits, valid for three years from 1 April 2020, to cover up to 90% of out-of-pocket expenses for enterprise and workforce transformation programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: This will benefit over 35,000 enterprises, which hire more than 1.5 million local workers.

sections.label: SME digital and growth support
sections.summary: A traditional logistics SME can get free Start Digital subscription, up to $30,000 Productivity Solutions Grant, up to $100,000 Market Readiness Assistance, and SkillsFuture support for up to 90% of course fees.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: For example, a traditional logistics SME can benefit from free subscription under the Start Digital pack for six months to access more customers through digital marketing and e-commerce; receive up to $30,000 in support from the Productivity Solutions Grant to implement inventory and fleet management solutions; enjoy up to $100,000 from the enhanced Market Readiness Assistance programme for each new market the business is expanding into; and also receive SkillsFuture support for up to 90% of course fees to upskill their employees.

sections.label: Enterprise Singapore project support
sections.summary: Enterprise Singapore supported over 13,000 projects from over 11,000 enterprises last year, generating $17.3 billion value-add and 21,700 new PMET jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Enterprise Singapore supported more than 13,000 projects from over 11,000 enterprises last year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: These will generate $17.3 billion in value-add and create 21,700 new PMET jobs and also positive outcomes for existing workers.

sections.label: SME Centres assistance in 2019
sections.summary: In 2019, the SME Centres assisted over 28,000 companies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: In 2019, the SME Centres assisted over 28,000 companies.

sections.label: Enterprise Leadership for Transformation programme
sections.summary: ESG will launch a three-year pilot Enterprise Leadership for Transformation programme later this year to support business leaders of promising SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Learning from the early success of Scale-up SG, ESG will launch a new Enterprise Leadership for Transformation (ELT) programme later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: ELT is a three-year pilot programme that supports business leaders of promising SMEs to achieve their next bound of growth.

sections.label: Funding for programme fees
sections.summary: Participating local enterprises will receive up to 90% funding support for their programme fees.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Participating local enterprises will receive up to 90% funding support for their programme fees.

sections.label: SinFooTech excise duty exemption
sections.summary: PEP and Singapore Customs agreed SinFooTech need not pay excise duties on research products not sold commercially, saving about $90,000 over six months.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: PEP and Singapore Customs worked together with the company, and after reviewing its proposal, Customs agreed that SinFooTech need not pay excise duties on its research products, as long as these are not sold commercially.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: This cost saving will be about $90,000 over six months for the company.

sections.label: HECS triple five target
sections.summary: HECS is challenged to achieve a triple five target in 2020, and HEUP will be introduced as an integrated support package for MAs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: For 2020, I have challenged the HECS to achieve a "triple five" stretched target: firstly, to partner at least five new precincts, in addition to the three they are supporting currently; secondly, to help 200 enterprises with their transformation and digitalisation, which is five times more than the 40 last year; and thirdly, to train 1,000 workers and shop owners, which is five times more than the 200 last year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We will introduce the Heartland Enterprise Upgrading Programme (HEUP) as a single integrated support package for MAs.

sections.label: Enhanced support for MAs
sections.summary: Funding for upgrading common areas rises from 80% to 90%, and the shop owner support threshold may be lowered from 100% to 75%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We will also provide enhanced support to MAs through the programme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We will also increase funding support for the upgrading of common areas from 80% to 90%, reducing the costs for shop owners.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: In addition, currently, under HDB's Revitalisation of Shops (ROS) scheme, the support of all shop owners is required for upgrading works to commence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We are considering amending the legislation to lower the threshold from 100% to 75%, to allow works to proceed if at least three quarters of the shop owners are supportive.

sections.label: ESG roadmaps and GlobalConnect@SBF
sections.summary: ESG started developing strategic roadmaps with TACs last year, and GlobalConnect@SBF will be launched this April.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: Last year, ESG started developing strategic roadmaps with our TACs to help them adopt longer-term plans to transform industry.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: As Minister Chan Chun Sing shared earlier, GlobalConnect@SBF will be launched this April.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: It will scale up SBF's capabilities and resources to help our Singapore-based companies access new markets overseas.

sections.label: Price Control Act against profiteering
sections.summary: Powers under the Price Control Act were recently exercised to ask two retailers that had received public complaints about profiteering.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan asked about errant retailers that attempted to profiteer from the COVID-19 situation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: We recently exercised our powers under the Price Control Act to ask two retailers which had received public complaints about profiteering.

sections.label: STEER programme and industry funds
sections.summary: STEER will match $1 for every $4 raised by industry-led funds up to $1 million per fund, with SFIC launching a members' assistance scheme.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: Last month, when demand surged for essential commodities, the Singapore Food Manufacturers' Association teamed up with six other associations to increase domestic food supply.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: E-commerce companies, with the help of ESG, shared delivery vans to cope with increased demand for delivery throughout Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: We will introduce the SG-Together Enhancing Enterprise Resilience (STEER) programme which will match $1 for every $4 raised by industry-led funds, up to $1 million per fund.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: The Singapore Furniture Industries Council will be launching its members' assistance scheme this week as part of this, supported by ESG through STEER, and more than 250 of their members will benefit from the scheme to strengthen business capabilities and market diversification.

sections.label: Retailer and landlord issues
sections.summary: There are some issues between retailers and the landlord, and a spectrum of responses has come to attention since rebates and help were announced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Yes, we are aware that there are some issues between the retailers and the landlord.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Since the Government announced the rebates and the help to the businesses, it has come to our attention that there is an entire spectrum of responses.

sections.label: ESG consults restaurant and retail associations
sections.summary: ESG is consulting the Restaurant Association of Singapore and the Singapore Retailers Association to help them work with major landlords.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: To this end, ESG is in close consultation with both the Restaurant Association of Singapore and also the Singapore Retailers Association (SRA) to help them work with the major landlords.

sections.label: Landlords passing benefits to tenants
sections.summary: It says landlords should pass some benefits to tenants rather than saving, for Singapore to continue doing well as One Team Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Only so can we continue to do well as One Team Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: It will be very shortsighted for landlords to try to stinge and save a bit here and there, instead of passing on some of the benefits to the tenants.

sections.label: Attribution of $17.3 billion value-add
sections.summary: It asks whether outcomes such as $17.3 billion in value-add are attributable solely to ESG support.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Is the claim that the outcomes, such as the $17.3 billion in value-add, attributable solely to ESG support?

sections.label: Public grants and TFP growth
sections.summary: It asks the extent to which public grant schemes have contributed to recent improvements in total factor productivity growth.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The second clarification is: what is the extent to which public grant schemes have contributed to recent improvements in total factor productivity (TFP) growth?

sections.label: TFP as residual indicator
sections.summary: It states TFP is a residual indicator, being the change in GDP not attributed to changes in capital and labour inputs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The issue of TFP, Sir, I must first qualify that even though I did some economics in school, my level of economics is nowhere near Assoc Prof Walter Theseira's.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But based on my understanding, TFP is a residual indicator, in the sense that you look at what is the change in GDP that is not attributed to changes in capital and labour inputs.

sections.label: Petrochemical industry worker numbers
sections.summary: Senior Minister of State Koh Poh Koon mentioned that 26,000 workers are currently employed in the petrochemical industry.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Senior Minister of State Koh Poh Koon mentioned that there are 26,000 workers currently employed in the petrochemical industry.
